text: One day, as the crowd pressed in on him to hear the word of God, Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret.
He saw two boats sitting by the lake; the fishermen had stepped out of them and were washing their nets.

versions.text: He saw two boats lying at the shore; the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.
versions.explanation: παρὰ τὴν λίμνην is "by the lake" (echoing verse 1), not "at the shore." Also, "had gone out of them" is awkward for oral reading; "had stepped out of them" renders ἀποβάντες more naturally.

text: He got into one of the boats, the one belonging to Simon, and asked him to put out a little from the land. Then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch."
Simon answered, "Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But at your word I will let down the nets."
When they had done so, they caught such a huge number of fish that their nets began to tear.
So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came, and together they filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell at Jesus' knees and said, "Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man."
For he and all who were with him were seized with amazement at the catch of fish they had taken,
and so were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. Then Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid. From now on you will be catching people."
So they brought their boats to shore, left everything behind, and followed him.
While Jesus was in one of the towns, there was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged him, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Jesus reached out his hand and touched him, saying, "I am willing. Be clean." And immediately the leprosy left him.
Jesus ordered him to tell no one, but said, "Go, show yourself to the priest, and make the offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
Yet the news about him spread all the more, and great crowds gathered to hear him and to be healed of their illnesses.
But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.

One day, as he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem, and the power of the Lord was with him to heal.
Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a bed, trying to bring him in and lay him before Jesus.
When they could find no way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles, right into the middle of the crowd in front of Jesus.

versions.text: When they could find no way to get him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the room, right in front of Jesus.
versions.explanation: The chain "lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the room, right in front of Jesus" piles up four prepositional phrases and reads awkwardly aloud. The Greek says simply "into the midst, before Jesus"; "the room" is an added detail, whereas the midst of the gathered crowd is what is in view.

text: Seeing their faith, he said, "Friend, your sins are forgiven."
The scribes and the Pharisees began to reason among themselves, "Who is this man who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
Jesus knew what they were thinking and answered them, "Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—he said to the paralyzed man, "I tell you, get up, take your mat, and go home."
At once the man stood up in front of them, picked up what he had been lying on, and went home praising God.
Amazement gripped them all, and they glorified God. Filled with awe, they said, "We have seen incredible things today."
After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. "Follow me," he said to him.
And Levi left everything, got up, and followed him.
Then Levi held a great banquet for Jesus at his house, and a large crowd of tax collectors and others were reclining at table with them.
But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to his disciples, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered them, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."
Then they said to him, "John's disciples fast often and offer prayers, and so do the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours go on eating and drinking."
Jesus said to them, "Can you make the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them?
But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them; then they will fast in those days."
He also told them a parable: "No one tears a patch from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

versions.text: He also told them a parable: "No one tears a patch from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he ruins the new garment, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
versions.explanation: σχίσει means "will tear" and deliberately repeats the verb σχίσας ("tears") from the first clause. "Ruins" loses that intentional word-play and weakens the point of the image.

text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins; the wine will spill out, and the skins will be ruined.
No, new wine must be poured into new wineskins.
And no one who has been drinking old wine wants the new, for he says, 'The old is good.'"
